name: Judy M Spak, MLS
title: Head of Academic Research and Education
bio: As Head of Academic Research and Education at the Cushing/Whitney Medical Library, I provide expert research assistance and collaborate with faculty and learners on a broad range of topics. I am particularly interested in health professions education scholarship and the role of librarians in teaching and assessing the evidence-based information-seeking skills of trainees. I collaborate on evidence and knowledge syntheses projects by providing expert searching and methodological expertise. The Academic Research and Education team supports the Yale School of Medicine, the Physician Associate program, the Yale School of Public Health, and the Yale School of Nursing and provides exceptional research and education services to the health sciences community at Yale. When not at work, I enjoy playing with my Pembroke Welsh Corgi, watching hockey, and knitting.

name: Alyssa Ann Grimshaw, MBA, MLIS, MPH
title: Biomedical Research and Methodology Librarian
bio: Alyssa Grimshaw is a Biomedical Research and Methodology Librarian. She earned a post-master's certificate as an interprofessional informationist at Simmons University School of Library and Information Sciences. As an information expert, she collaborates on evidence synthesis and meta-research projects. Her research interests include reproducibility, reporting, and housing impacts on public health. Alyssa provides in-­depth reference, information, research and consultation services for clinical professionals and users in the health sciences community, including literature searches in support of systematic reviews, research, grants, clinical practice, animal use, teaching, and publishing.

name: Caitlin Meyer, MLS
title: Research and Education Librarian
bio: Caitlin Meyer is a librarian at Yale’s Harvey Cushing/John Hay Whitney Medical Library. She coordinates the library’s instruction program and supports the students and faculty of the School of Medicine’s Physician Associate Program and Physician Assistant Online Program. Caitlin has a Master of Library and Information Science degree from UCLA and a Bachelor’s degree in Communication Studies from Vanderbilt. Outside of work, Caitlin is an avid hiker, camper, and fan of bluegrass music.

name: Kate Nyhan, MLS
title: Research and Education Librarian
bio: Kate Nyhan is a research and education librarian for public health at Cushing/Whitney Medical Library and a lecturer in environmental health sciences at Yale School of Public Health. She earned a post-master's certificate as an interprofessional informationist at Simmons University School of Library and Information Sciences. As an information expert, she contributes to evidence synthesis and metaresearch projects. Her research interests include research waste, reproducibility, reporting, and the information behavior of the public health workforce.

name: Madison Jurgens
title: Biomedical Research and Methodology Librarian
bio: Madison supports Yale School of Medicine affiliates by providing research consultations, developing educational programs, and participating in collaborative projects. She specializes in evidence synthesis methodologies, such as systematic and scoping reviews and offers expert guidance throughout the research lifecycle, from research conceptualization to preparing manuscripts for publication. Madison holds a Master of Library and Information Science (MLIS) from San José State University and a BA in Anthropology from the University of California, Irvine. Prior to joining Yale, she served as an Informationist at Columbia University Irving Medical Center and as an Information Desk and Departmental Library Intern at the University of Pennsylvania.

name: Alexandria Leigh Brackett, MLIS, MA
title: Research & Education Nursing Librarian
bio: Alexandria provides in-­depth reference, education, and research consultation services for Yale School of Nursing and clinical nurses at Yale New Haven Hospital.

name: Zsuzsanna Nemeth, MLIS
title: Head of Clinical Research and Education
bio: Zsuzsanna Nemeth is Head of Clinical Research and Education at the Cushing/Whitney Medical Library. She leads a team of librarians who provide services and build partnerships supporting clinical care, research, and education across Yale New Haven Health System and the Yale School of Medicine. Working closely with clinicians, trainees, faculty, and health-system colleagues, Zsuzsanna helps connect care teams with timely, evidence-based information and specialized library expertise. Her work supports informed clinical decision-making, lifelong learning, and the integration of high-quality evidence into patient care.

name: Melissa C Funaro, MLS, MS
title: Clinical Research and Education Librarian
bio: I am a Clinical Librarian at the Cushing/Whitney Medical Library dedicated to serving the research needs of the Medical Campus. I am a point of contact for all things library, including support for literature searching and citation management software programs such as EndNote. Please contact me with your questions.

name: Casey Phillips, MLIS, AHIP
title: Clinical Research and Education Librarian
bio: Casey Phillips, MLIS, AHIP, is a Clinical Research and Education Librarian for the Cushing/Whitney Medical Library at Yale University. She provides training, consultation, and literature searches in support of evidence synthesis reviews, patient care, clinical research, animal welfare, and grants. Casey is an active contributor to the health sciences library profession, having served in leadership and volunteer roles within chapters of the Medical Library Association, including her current service with the North Atlantic Health Sciences Libraries Chapter (NAHSL).

name: Carly Schanock, MLIS
title: Clinical Research and Education Librarian

contact.location: Harvey Cushing/John Hay Whitney Medical Library

bio: Carly Schanock is a Clinical Research and Education Librarian specializing in artificial intelligence (AI) applications in clinical research, clinical practice, and scholarly communication. Her other work centers on evidence synthesis, including systematic and scoping reviews, clinical practice guidelines, and advanced literature searching. She collaborates with researchers and healthcare professionals throughout the research lifecycle, providing expertise in information retrieval, evidence-based decision-making, and emerging technologies. Their teaching and consultation activities focus on helping learners and investigators effectively evaluate, integrate, and apply AI and information resources to support research, publishing, and patient care. In winter 2027, they are starting an AI Applications for Health Sciences online graduate certificate at Northeastern University's Bouvé College of Health Sciences

name: Justin DeMayo
title: Emerging Technologies Engineer
bio: Justin supports the medical library’s researchers, staff, and mission by exploring emerging technologies and engineering the systems and applications that put them to use, spanning infrastructure, access, reliability, and application development. His focus includes cloud infrastructure, automation, and evaluating and applying AI and other emerging technologies to support the medical school’s mission.

A certified Carpentries instructor, Justin teaches courses on computational foundations, including the command line, Git and GitHub, Python and data analysis, reproducible containers, and AI tools for research. Justin is interested in AI and computational methods in support of research. His applied work spans data engineering, automation, and AI, including the development and evaluation of agentic AI systems, with a focus on transparency and reproducibility.

name: Sofia Fertuzinhos, PhD
title: Research & Education Librarian for Bioinformatics
bio: Sofia Fertuzinhos, PhD, is the Research and Education Librarian for Bioinformatics at Yale’s Harvey Cushing/John Hay Whitney Medical Library. She provides individualized bioinformatics support and consulting to basic and biomedical researchers, helping them navigate biological databases, plan sequencing projects, analyze next-generation sequencing data, and use computational tools for gene annotation, transcriptomics, pathway analysis, visualization, and reproducible research.

Sofia earned a joint PhD in Biochemistry from Yale University and the University of Coimbra, graduating summa cum laude. Her doctoral and postdoctoral research at Yale focused on neuroscience and the development of neural cell types, integrating molecular, cellular, and systems-level approaches.
Sofia helps researchers make rigorous and effective use of Yale’s bioinformatics and research-computing resources.

name: Rolando Garcia-Milian, MLS, AHIP
title: Biomedical Sciences Research Support Librarian and Lecturer in Epidemiology
bio: Rolando Garcia-Milian is a bioinformatics professional who serves as a member of the Bioinformatics Support Hub, Cushing/Whitney Medical Library, and the Yale/NIDA Neuroproteomics Center at Yale School of Medicine. He also lectures in Epidemiology for the Environmental Health Sciences Department at Yale School of Public Health. Rolando began his academic journey at the University of Havana, where he earned a degree in biology and worked on the molecular basis of Human Papillomavirus-associated diseases, such as cervical cancer, regarding their response to cytokines. At Yale School of Medicine, he offers comprehensive bioinformatics support on omics data analysis, including training, consultation, and collaboration on various research projects. With authorship or co-authorship of over 70 research papers and book chapters, Rolando is extensively published in his field. Outside of his professional life, he enjoys gardening, fine arts, reading, running, and hiking.

name: Maximilian Wegener, MPH
title: Biomedical Informatics Librarian
bio: Max Wegener is a Biomedical Informatics Librarian specializing in research data, programming, and computational methods for biomedical and public health research. An epidemiologist by training, he brings more than a decade of experience in infectious disease surveillance and HIV/hepatitis C research to his work with Yale investigators. His work centers on helping researchers find, retrieve, clean, analyze, and share data, including large clinical and population datasets such as the NIH All of Us Research Program. He collaborates with faculty, staff, and students throughout the research lifecycle, providing expertise in R programming, statistical analysis, reproducible research practices, and data retrieval through APIs and web scraping. His teaching and consultation activities focus on building practical, hands-on data skills, including AI-assisted coding, supported by free, open training materials he develops for learners at Yale and beyond.

name: Marika Basagoitia, MS
title: Librarian, Web Services
bio: Marika is responsible for developing, maintaining, and improving the library’s digital presence and user experience. She earned her Master of Science in Computer Science from the University of Colorado Boulder.
